description: READ A TABLE, rows under their column names («Clasa: 2110 | CAEN Rev. 2: Fabricarea produselor farmaceutice de bază»), with the id of every cell, the row's place in the table (section, parent codes) and the title and act of the table. A page is bounded and the answer states the total and the exact call for the next page; nothing is cut in silence. Pick rows by number (`rows`), a window around a cell or a row (`around`), the rows that contain a text (`find`), only some columns (`columns`), and a format (`rows`, `markdown`, `csv`, `json`). A table of tens of thousands of cells is read by range.

around.description: A cell id ('cell:19612089') or a row number ('304'): the rows around it, `radius` on each side.

columns.description: Show only these columns: names or numbers, comma separated ('Clasa,CAEN Rev. 2' or '0-3').

cursor.description: The last row number already read: the page starts after it. The answer prints the call for the next page.

find.description: Only the rows where a cell contains this text (case and diacritics ignored).

find_column.description: Look for `find` in this column only: its name or number.

ids.description: true: print the id of every cell under each row.

limit.description: Rows on a page, 1-200 (default 40). Keep it the same between pages.

paths.description: true: print each row's place (section, parent codes) after it, even on a long page.

radius.description: Rows on each side of `around` (default 3), or around each `find` match (default 3, 0 for none).

rows.description: Row numbers as the answers print them: '304', '300-310' or '1-50,304'. Without it, the page starts at the first data row.

table.description: The table, as list_tables or search_tables printed it: 'tabel:14164713.0' (or just 14164713 when the node holds one table).

name: read_table
